entities.summary:
Cheng Pu (b. 200 CE, Fengrun District) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Fengrun District.

    Known in the fields of military leaders & commanders, his contributions to the administration of the Three Kingdoms (220–280 CE) shaped the regional dynamics of ancient China.

    Cheng Pu's legacy extends to the Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), where his expertise in governance and strategic planning influenced the development of the imperial system.

    The enduring impact of Cheng Pu's work can be seen in the modern-day governance structures of China, with many of his ideas incorporated into the country's administrative systems.
